protocol.description:
This protocol allows clients to ask the compositor to provide a buffer containing the contents of capture image sources so that it can attach them to its own surfaces.
Instead of the client capturing and rendering the contents into its own buffer, this protocol moves the heavy work of rendering a capture source to the compositor. The client requests a render, gets the buffer for that render, and attaches that buffer to a surface that it owns. The compositor then fills in the contents of that buffer with the requested capture source. The compositor is responsible for keeping the content of that source up to date in the buffer as it changes.
The contents of the buffer are never sent to the host client. Only the compositor sees these contents.
The protocol relies on ext_image_capture_source_v1.
The compositor may choose to restrict this protocol to a special client launched by the compositor itself or expose it to all clients, this is compositor policy.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: ext_image_render_capture_manager_v1
interface.description:
A client uses the image capture embedding manager to request a new embedding.
An embedding is created from an ext_image_capture_source_v1. This source can be backed by anything including outputs, groups of surfaces, an individual surface, etc.
If the manager is destroyed, new embeddings will not be created, but existing embeddings remain valid up until the point of their destruction.

request.name: create_embedding

description.summary: create embedding for image capture source

request.description: Creates an embedding for the image capture source.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request should be called when the client will no longer use the ext_image_render_capture_manager. Afterward, no new embeddings can be created, but existing embeddings remain valid up until the point of their destruction.

interface.name: ext_image_render_capture_v1
interface.description:
An ext_image_render_capture_v1 object is used to render the the image capture source that it was created with inside of a surface owned by the client.
The image capture source is not mapped to a surface when the object is created. The client must call obtain the buffer via get_buffer, attach the buffer to a surface, and commit the surface for the mapping to occur. The surface of the client is subject to the wl_subsurface synchronization model.
The client itself never sees the contents of this surface. Instead, the content is entirely rendered into the provided buffer by the compositor.
The content of the buffer must automatically be updated by the compositor as the source image changes.

request.name: get_buffer

description.summary: retrieve buffer for image capture source

request.description:
Retrieve a buffer for the image capture source that this embedding was created with.
This buffer must be attached to a surface and that surface must be committed for the mapping to be finalized.
This must be called by the client following a size event in order to update the buffer to the new size.
Calling this while a buffer already exists for this embedding raises a buffer_active error.

event.name: size

description.summary: send when the size of the image capture source changes

event.description:
This is sent when the size of the image capture source changes.
The client should destroy any buffer that they are already holding and make the get_buffer request in response to this event. If the client does not do this, then their embedding will cease updating.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Signals that the embedding should be destroyed.
